plain_cards.front: Aerodynamic drag force and required power scale with speed v how?
plain_cards.back: Drag force F ∝ v²; required power P = F·v ∝ v³ (doubling speed multiplies drag 4× and power 8×).
plain_cards.source_note: Standard physical scaling law / SI unit conversion

plain_cards.front: Square-cube law: if you double a structure's linear dimensions, what happens to surface area and mass?
plain_cards.back: Surface area scales 4× (L²); volume and mass scale 8× (L³) — why elephants have pillar legs and small animals lose heat fast.
plain_cards.source_note: Standard physical scaling law / SI unit conversion

plain_cards.front: Radiative heat emission (Stefan–Boltzmann) scales with absolute temperature T how?
plain_cards.back: P ∝ T⁴ (in Kelvin). Doubling absolute temperature increases thermal radiation 16×.
plain_cards.source_note: Standard physical scaling law / SI unit conversion

plain_cards.front: Characteristic diffusion time t across distance L scales how?
plain_cards.back: t ≈ L² / D (scales with the SQUARE of distance — fast across a 1 µm cell, hopelessly slow across 1 cm).
plain_cards.source_note: Standard physical scaling law / SI unit conversion

plain_cards.front: Decibels (dB): what power/intensity multiplier corresponds to +3 dB and +10 dB?
plain_cards.back: +3 dB ≈ 2× power; +10 dB = 10× power (+20 dB = 100×; perceived loudness doubles roughly every +10 dB).
plain_cards.source_note: Standard physical scaling law / SI unit conversion

plain_cards.front: Carnot maximum heat-engine efficiency formula (temperatures in Kelvin)?
plain_cards.back: η_max = 1 − T_cold / T_hot. At 300 K ambient and 600 K steam, absolute ceiling is 50%.
plain_cards.source_note: Standard physical scaling law / SI unit conversion

plain_cards.front: 1 kilowatt-hour (kWh) equals how many megajoules (MJ) and kilocalories?
plain_cards.back: 1 kWh = 3.6 MJ ≈ 860 kcal (a human's ~2,000 kcal daily food intake is only ~2.3 kWh!).
plain_cards.source_note: Standard physical scaling law / SI unit conversion

plain_cards.front: Water specific heat capacity and latent heat of vaporization?
plain_cards.back: Specific heat = 4.18 kJ/(kg·K); latent heat of vaporization = 2,260 kJ/kg (~5.4× the energy to heat water from 0→100 °C).
plain_cards.source_note: Standard physical scaling law / SI unit conversion

plain_cards.front: Solar irradiance at top of atmosphere vs. peak clear noon vs. 24-hour global surface mean?
plain_cards.back: Top of atmosphere = 1,361 W/m²; peak sea-level noon ≈ 1,000 W/m²; 24-hour global average ≈ 180–200 W/m².
plain_cards.source_note: Standard physical scaling law / SI unit conversion

plain_cards.front: Wind turbine available power scales with rotor diameter D and wind speed v how?
plain_cards.back: P = ½ ρ A v³ ∝ D² v³ — a 26% higher wind speed roughly DOUBLES available power.
plain_cards.source_note: Standard physical scaling law / SI unit conversion

plain_cards.front: Speed-of-sound distance rule for lightning/thunder?
plain_cards.back: Sound travels ~343 m/s → ~3 seconds per kilometer, ~5 seconds per mile.
plain_cards.source_note: Standard physical scaling law / SI unit conversion

plain_cards.front: Hydrostatic water pressure increases by ~1 atmosphere every how many meters of depth?
plain_cards.back: ~10 meters (33 ft) of water adds ~1 atm (100 kPa / 14.7 psi). At 100 m depth, total pressure is ~11 atm.
plain_cards.source_note: Standard physical scaling law / SI unit conversion

plain_cards.front: Rule of 72 (and Rule of 115): doubling and tripling time at r% compounding?
plain_cards.back: Doubling time ≈ 72 / r (at 7% → ~10.3 yr). Tripling time ≈ 115 / r. (Exact: ln 2 ≈ 0.693).
plain_cards.source_note: Standard physical scaling law / SI unit conversion

plain_cards.front: How many seconds are in one year (Fermi anchor)?
plain_cards.back: ≈ π × 10^7 seconds (exact: 3.1557 × 10^7 s, within 0.45% of π × 10^7).
plain_cards.source_note: Standard physical scaling law / SI unit conversion

plain_cards.front: Quick 95% confidence margin of error for a random poll of size N?
plain_cards.source_note: Standard physical scaling law / SI unit conversion

plain_cards.front: 1 acre in square feet and hectares?
plain_cards.back: 1 acre = 43,560 sq ft (≈ 209 ft × 209 ft, roughly a football field without end zones) ≈ 0.405 hectares (1 ha = 10,000 m²).
plain_cards.source_note: Standard physical scaling law / SI unit conversion

plain_cards.front: Converting meters per second (m/s) to mph and km/h?
plain_cards.source_note: Standard physical scaling law / SI unit conversion

plain_cards.front: HVAC cooling '1 Ton of Refrigeration' equals how many BTU/hr and kW thermal?
plain_cards.back: 1 ton = 12,000 BTU/hr ≈ 3.52 kW thermal (rate needed to melt 1 short ton of ice over 24 hours).
plain_cards.source_note: Standard physical scaling law / SI unit conversion

plain_cards.front: Room temperature (~20 °C / 68 °F) in Kelvin, and thermal energy k_B T in eV?
plain_cards.back: ~293 K (~300 K Fermi anchor); k_B T ≈ 0.026 eV (1/40 eV).
plain_cards.source_note: Standard physical scaling law / SI unit conversion

plain_cards.front: Volume of 1 mole of any ideal gas at STP (0 °C, 1 atm)?
plain_cards.back: 22.4 liters (at room temp 25 °C: ~24.5 L). Air mean molar mass ≈ 29 g/mol → 29 g / 24 L ≈ 1.2 kg/m³.
plain_cards.source_note: Standard physical scaling law / SI unit conversion
